logic.reason: Gout comes in attacks of a hot, red, swollen joint that build quickly and then settle.
A gout attack makes the joint swollen, hot and red within a day.

name: Inflammatory arthritis (such as rheumatoid arthritis)
description: The immune system inflames the lining of several joints, often the small joints of both hands and feet on both sides. Joints are swollen, warm and stiff for well over half an hour in the morning. Early treatment by a rheumatologist protects the joints, so see a doctor if this sounds like you.

logic.reason: The disease usually affects several joints, often the same ones on both sides.
Inflamed joint linings stiffen overnight and take a long time to loosen.
Inflamed joint linings make the joints swell.
Inflamed joints swell and can feel warm.

name: Joint infection (septic arthritis), including spread of gonorrhoea to the joints
description: Bacteria get into a joint, usually through the blood, and quickly make it hot, swollen and very painful, often with fever. Gonorrhoea can spread through the blood to several joints and tendon sheaths at once, with a few spots on the skin. An infected joint can be damaged within days, so get seen the same day.

logic.reason: Joint pain and a history of joint swelling are the only findings present in most adults with a bacterial joint infection (swelling in 78%).
Fever was present in 57%, so it fits but its absence doesn't rule an infection out.
Diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis, joint surgery, a hip or knee replacement, skin infection and HIV each made a joint infection more likely.
The common form of spread gonorrhoea is a triad of joint pain moving between joints, skin spots and inflamed tendon sheaths.
Skin spots are part of the triad of spread gonorrhoea.

name: Reactive arthritis: joint inflammation after a gut or urinary infection
description: Days to weeks after a bout of diarrhoea or a urinary or genital infection, the immune system inflames a few joints, usually in the legs and on one side more than the other, and often the heel or the tendon attachments. The eyes may be red and the urine may burn. A doctor can test for the infection and treat the inflammation.

logic.reason: A preceding infection is a main criterion: diarrhoea, or burning or discharge when passing urine, from 3 days to 6 weeks before the arthritis.
It is an arthritis, usually of one to a few joints, so swelling is expected.
Conjunctivitis was reported in 51% of patients, mostly in the acute form.
It usually affects one to a few joints on one side more than the other; many swollen joints on both sides point to another kind of arthritis.

name: Polymyalgia rheumatica
description: An inflammatory condition of people over 50 that causes aching and marked stiffness of both shoulders, the neck and often both hips, worst in the morning. It responds quickly to steroid tablets prescribed by a doctor. It can come with giant cell arteritis: a new headache, scalp tenderness, jaw pain on chewing or any change in vision needs same-day medical care.

context.text: In the study behind the classification criteria (people 50 or older with new pain in both shoulders), a score of 4 or more picked out 68% of those with polymyalgia rheumatica and wrongly included 22% of those with look-alike conditions: 12% of shoulder problems but 35% of rheumatoid arthritis. The authors state the criteria are not meant for diagnosis.

criteria.title: 2012 EULAR/ACR classification criteria for polymyalgia rheumatica (needs age 50 or older, both shoulders aching and raised inflammation blood tests; then 4 or more points)

items.prompt: Aged 50 or older (required)
Aching in both shoulders (required)
Morning stiffness lasting more than 45 minutes (2 points)
Hip pain or limited hip movement (1 point)
No pain in other joints (1 point)

clinicianOnly: Raised CRP and/or ESR (blood tests; required)
Rheumatoid factor and ACPA both negative (blood tests; 2 points)

logic.reason: The aching and stiffness affect both shoulders, and often the neck and both hips.

name: Fibromyalgia (widespread pain from an oversensitive pain system)
description: Long-lasting widespread pain on both sides of the body, above and below the waist, with tiredness, unrefreshing sleep and poor concentration. No joint or muscle is damaged; the nervous system turns up pain signals. It is diagnosed from the pattern of symptoms after other causes are excluded.

logic.reason: The pain affects many parts of the body on both sides.
The fibromyalgia survey criteria count how many body areas are painful, so the pain is widespread by definition.
The same criteria score tiredness, unrefreshing sleep and thinking problems alongside the pain.

name: Sensitised pain system (nociplastic pain)
description: The pain system itself has become oversensitive and stays turned up: the nervous system amplifies signals, so ordinary touch, movement or pressure can hurt although no tissue is being damaged and no nerve is trapped. It can follow an injury that has healed, come on gradually, or sit on top of another painful problem, and it can affect one region or many (fibromyalgia is the best-known widespread form). The pain is real. There is no scan or blood test for it: it is recognised by its pattern.

context.text: Under the IASP criteria, pain from damaged tissue or a nerve problem doesn't rule out an oversensitive pain system: more than one type of pain can be present at the same time.

context.text: The criteria were published in 2021 and have not yet been tested for accuracy; the review's authors call such studies urgently needed.

criteria.title: IASP clinical criteria for nociplastic pain (2021): 'possible' needs the first three items and a clinician's judgement; 'probable' needs all five

items.prompt: Pain for at least 3 months (required)
Pain spread over a region rather than one discrete spot (required)
Signs of pain hypersensitivity in the painful area, such as pain from a light brush (a clinician examines this; the home stroke test stands in for it)
Sensitivity to touch, movement, pressure or heat/cold in the painful area (for 'probable')
At least one of: sensitivity to sound, light or smells; sleep with frequent waking; tiredness or thinking problems (for 'probable')

clinicianOnly: Pain that tissue damage or a nerve problem can't entirely explain (required). The app only approximates this: the option comes first only when no tissue or nerve option explains your answers better.
Signs of pain hypersensitivity on examination (required for 'possible')

Pain in many body regions is one of the signs a trial physician used to recognise centralised pain.
Pain that began around particularly stressful life events is one of the signs a trial physician used to recognise centralised pain.
Pain that spreads to different areas over time is one of the signs a trial physician used to recognise centralised pain.

Pain that behaves inconsistently (shifting around, varying a lot through the day, easing with distraction, flaring only after an activity) is one of the signs a trial physician used to recognise centralised pain.
Pain set off by things that can't harm tissue (sounds, lights, smells, screens, anticipated stress, imagined movement) is one of the signs a trial physician used to recognise centralised pain.

mechanism.text: One model of how the pain system gets stuck: expecting damage makes harmless signals from the body feel painful, the pain then feels threatening, and that threat turns the pain up further, a loop that can keep pain going after an injury has healed.

name: Complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS)
description: Continuing pain in an arm or leg, usually after an injury, fracture or operation, that is far worse or lasts far longer than the injury explains. The nervous system and the blood vessels and skin of the limb react abnormally, so the limb can also change colour or temperature, swell, sweat differently, stiffen, or grow hair and nails differently. It is diagnosed by a clinician from symptoms and examination signs once other causes are excluded; early treatment matters.

context.text: Applied by clinicians with an examination, the Budapest criteria picked out 99% of people with CRPS and correctly excluded 68% of people with other nerve pain.

criteria.title: Budapest clinical criteria for CRPS: pain out of proportion, plus symptoms in at least three of the four groups (and examination signs a clinician checks)

items.prompt: Continuing pain out of proportion to any event that set it off (required)
Sensory: increased sensitivity, or pain from light touch
Vasomotor: temperature difference, or skin colour change or difference
Sudomotor/oedema: swelling, or sweating change or difference
Motor/trophic: less movement, weakness, tremor or abnormal postures, or hair, nail or skin changes

clinicianOnly: At least one examination sign in two or more of the four groups (required)
No other diagnosis better explains the signs and symptoms (required)

logic.reason: It usually starts after an injury, a fracture or an operation on the limb, though it can follow a minor one.

name: Ankle impingement (tissue pinched at the front or back of the ankle joint)
description: Thickened scar tissue, a bony spur or a small extra bone (os trigonum) gets pinched between the ankle bones at the end of the ankle's movement: at the front or front-outer side when the foot bends fully up, often after a sprain, or at the back when the foot points hard down, as in dancers and downhill runners.

context.text: Front and front-outer impingement often follow ankle sprains; the typical story is chronic pain at the front of the ankle, worse when the foot bends up, with tenderness at the front of the ankle.

Back-of-ankle impingement is deep pain at the back of the ankle brought on by pointing the foot down, most common in ballet dancers, footballers and downhill runners; the exact spot is often hard to point to. No study has reported how accurate the pointing-down test is.

mechanism.text: Soft tissue (scarred or thickened joint lining or ligament) or bone (spurs, an os trigonum or a long back process of the talus) is squeezed between the shin bone and the talus at the end of the ankle's movement: at the front when the foot bends up, at the back when it points down. Fractures, sprains and long-term overuse start it.

logic.reason: The tissue is pinched only when the joint closes at the end of its movement, so pain at the front when the foot bends up, or at the back when it points down, is the defining feature.
